affected_predicate.description: The account olivia@10.0.2.2 from muted_accounts.csv is imported into the @test@10.0.2.2 account's muted list with the file's hide-notifications setting applied.

competing_trace_defects.description: After reaching the Mastodon Settings screen, the trace performs a static scroll and then leaves without opening the visible @test@10.0.2.2 account settings, abandoning a relevant navigation path.

The trace repeatedly treats profile-screen controls as possible settings entry points even after they visibly open the profile sharing sheet or handle explanation, producing repeated unrelated interactions.

chains.rationale: At the reuse target, the prediction explicitly adopts the reused account-name attempt as a failed premise and navigates back, which visibly exits Mastodon to the launcher and creates an off-track detour. The trace then corrects that detour by reopening Mastodon, selecting Home, using the actual Home-screen settings control, and entering @test account settings. Thus the target-linked navigation defect is recovered and does not remain continuous. Subsequent screens inspect Filters and Privacy and reach, but no supplied screen shows olivia@10.0.2.2 in a muted list or otherwise exposes the import state, so the affected predicate is not observable.

summary: The sole strict-MHR reuse visibly produces a temporary off-track exit from Mastodon after preserving the account-name navigation premise. That mechanism is later corrected when the trace reaches the real Home-screen settings path. The supplied terminal screens do not expose whether the CSV account was imported. Independent prefix defects include prematurely abandoning the initially reached Settings screen and a repeated profile-sharing navigation loop.
